text:
Nina: following up from the refactor RFC  proposal: extract token/accounting logic out of the router into a lightweight TokenAccounting service. sketch and risk list below.

Omar: motivation? speed of router or easier billing ops?

Nina: both. router's hot path has grown complex (decode -> route -> auth -> count -> quota). During spikes counting causes tail latency and noisy CPU. Billing also needs auditable events.

Liu: key question: how strict does quota enforcement need to remain? If we go async we risk overshoot.

Sanjay: product: throttles must react within ~1s for interactive tiers. Billing invoices ok with eventual reconciliation. So hybrid model makes sense.

Nina: hybrid idea: keep a tiny fast path in router that consults a local lease/cache (Lease.check(client, tokens)) to decide immediate throttling. All calls also emit an event to TokenAccounting.ingest for durable accounting. For edge cases near limit, router hits TokenAccounting.sync_reserve(request_id, tokens) which is low-latency and strongly consistent.

Omar: implies router needs a small token-bucket per tenant with conservative limits and short TTLs. How do we avoid divergence between lease and authoritative counters?

Liu: plan: authoritative store is append-only event stream (Kafka) + compacted aggregates in a sharded store. TokenAccounting will maintain a per-tenant committed counter and expose a fast gRPC sync_reserve service. Router's local bucket is a hint and falls back to sync_reserve if unsure.

Sanjay: operationally we need clear failure modes. If TokenAccounting is slow/unreachable, do we fail-open, fail-closed, or degrade?

Nina: default: fail-open with a "metering-uncertain" tag and increment an incident metric. For enterprise tenants with strict SLAs, support opt-in strict mode that fails-closed to protect spend.

Omar: event model: router must emit idempotent events with request-id and sha256 of payload to allow dedupe. TokenAccounting.ingest consumes, writes to log, and updates aggregates asynchronously. We'll keep a replayable commit log for reconciliation.

Liu: suggestion: use topic partitioning by tenant-id and produce with acks=all. Consumers should checkpoint offsets externally for safe replay. Add a sequence number per request to help ordering.

Sanjay: reconciliation window / customer comms? Product ok with up to 48h reconcile for usage adjustments. Need public-facing doc and internal operations playbook for reconciliations.

Nina: cutover phases (rough):
1) Emit-only: router starts producing accounting events, still authoritative inline counting.
2) Read-replica: TokenAccounting builds aggregates and exposes read-only aggregate API for dashboards.
3) Partial sync-reserve: enable sync_reserve for 10% of tenants behind flag.
4) Roll forward: increase sync-reserve coverage, monitor divergence metrics.
5) Retire inline counting after 2 weeks of stability.

Omar: metrics to track: per-tenant divergence (router-inline - tokenaccounting-aggregate), lost-events rate, ingest-latency P50/P95/P99, sync_reserve latency, consumer lag.

Liu: SLO targets proposal: sync_reserve P50 < 4ms, P99 < 15ms; ingest end-to-end durability ack < 2s for 99.9%; consumer processing lag < 10s for 99.9%.

Sanjay: security: events contain billing-sensitive counts. Require mTLS between services, signed event envelope (HMAC with rotating keys), and immutable audit log retention policy. Also add an admin-only snapshot endpoint for auditors.

Nina: deploy model: TokenAccounting is a separate k8s service deployed as stateful set with partitioned shards (hash by tenant namespace). Autoscale consumers separately. We'll start with 2 shards and scale.

Omar: backpressure: if consumers fall behind, the router must apply backpressure via throttling or switch to conservative local buckets. We'll expose a circuit-breaker control to oncall that can shift to permissive or strict modes per shard.

Liu: dev experience: SDK should start adding X-Req-Id and X-Tenant-Trace headers to help dedupe and lineage. Provide a small client library for emitting idempotent event envelopes.

Sanjay: product asks: how do we surface near-real-time counters to customers? Provide a "usage-streaming" websocket for dashboard tiers (best-effort) and a read-API for aggregates. Make sure SLA caveats are documented.

Nina: additional migration notes: events must be backward compatible. We'll version event schema (v1 -> v2) and accept both for 90 days. Add a migration-run that replays router-produced events into the new system to seed aggregates.

Omar: recovery: provide a manual replay command that consumes a time range from Kafka and recomputes aggregates into a reconcile DB for audits.

Liu: operational dashboards: consumer lag heatmap, per-tenant divergence alert, per-shard cpu/memory, sync_reserve error budget burn. Add runbook steps for "excess divergence" including immediate rollback to inline counting for impacted tenants.

Sanjay: thumbs up. We'll prepare customer comms and a short FAQ. Also need a billing team sign-off on reconciliation policy.

deploy-bot: deploy requested: feature/token-accounting -> staging (ci-7890) :rocket:

Nina: I'll draft the cutover playbook and runbook. tagging @Omar for partition design and @Liu for SLO/consumer ops. Expect RFC update tomorrow: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/3976543210-token-accounting-extract (draft).
